purpose: Define all core service/system pages for SIPANEL industrial envelope expertise.

global_rules.positioning: SIPANEL is not a sandwich panel supplier only. It is an engineering-first industrial envelope systems company.
content_rules: Use engineering logic before marketing language.
Connect every service to risk reduction, material optimization, waterproofing, or execution control.
Each page must include a conversion CTA and RFQ path.
Each page must include internal links to related systems, case studies, and resources.

mobile_rules: Use horizontal swipe cards for applications and case studies.

seo.title: Sandwich Panel Systems | SIPANEL Engineering-Controlled Execution
seo.meta_description: SIPANEL engineers sandwich panel systems through precise layout, smart procurement, waterproofing logic, and controlled installation for industrial buildings.

hero.h1: Panel Layout, Waterproofing, and Installation — Reviewed Before Procurement.
hero.subheadline: SIPANEL identifies panel selection risks, flashing coordination gaps, and quantity errors before materials are ordered — reducing leakage, waste, and site rework.
hero.visual_direction: real sandwich panel industrial building, technical grid overlay, shop drawing detail preview

problem_context.title: Most Panel Problems Begin Before Installation.
cards: Incorrect panel selection for climate or application
Poor coordination between supplier and installer
Material waste from inaccurate quantity planning
Leakage risk from weak flashing and joint details
Project delays caused by missing accessories or unclear drawings

engineering_approach.title: How SIPANEL Controls Panel System Risk

steps.title: Panel System Review
steps.description: Project drawings, envelope requirements, insulation needs, and site conditions are reviewed before procurement.

steps.title: Shop Drawing Coordination
steps.description: Panel layout, cut lists, joint logic, accessories, and installation sequence are clarified before execution.

steps.title: Smart Procurement Planning
steps.description: Quantities, flashings, fasteners, trims, and accessories are planned to reduce waste and site delays.

steps.title: Controlled Installation
steps.description: Execution follows coordinated drawings, inspection checkpoints, and waterproofing detail logic.

quality_checkpoints: Panel thickness and core type verification

faq.question: How does SIPANEL select the right panel type for a project?
faq.answer: Panel type, insulation core (PIR, PUR, mineral wool, EPS), and thickness are reviewed based on project climate, structural loads, fire regulations, and intended use.

faq.question: How is roof leakage risk controlled in sandwich panel systems?
faq.answer: Roof slope, drainage paths, flashing details, joint sealing, and installation sequence are reviewed and coordinated before panels are procured.

faq.question: Does SIPANEL prepare shop drawings before procurement?
faq.answer: Yes. Panel layout, cut lists, flashing positions, accessory quantities, and installation sequence are documented in shop drawings before materials are ordered.

faq.question: How does SIPANEL reduce material waste?
faq.answer: Through coordinated layout planning, accurate BOM extraction, cut list optimization, and accessory quantity verification before procurement.

faq.question: Does SIPANEL work with specific panel manufacturers?
faq.answer: SIPANEL is not tied to a single manufacturer. Panel brand and specification are recommended based on project requirements, not supplier agreements.

faq.question: What happens during the engineering review?
faq.answer: Project drawings, envelope requirements, insulation needs, waterproofing logic, and site conditions are reviewed. A coordinated execution plan is prepared before procurement.

faq.question: Can SIPANEL coordinate procurement and accessories?
faq.answer: Yes. Panels, flashings, fasteners, trims, sealants, and ridge/eave accessories are planned together to prevent site delays and missing components.

faq.question: Does SIPANEL only supply panels or also handle installation?
faq.answer: SIPANEL provides engineering-controlled execution — from system review and shop drawings through procurement coordination and controlled installation.

conversion_cta.headline: Identify Panel System Risks Before Procurement Starts.
conversion_cta.text: Send project drawings or scope details. SIPANEL reviews panel selection, layout coordination, and waterproofing logic before materials are ordered.

seo.title: Standing Seam & ZIP Tech Roofing | SIPANEL Waterproof Roofing Systems
seo.meta_description: SIPANEL designs and executes standing seam and ZIP Tech roofing systems with waterproofing logic, drainage coordination, and controlled installation.

hero.h1: Standing Seam Roofing Built Around Waterproofing Logic.
hero.subheadline: SIPANEL coordinates roof slope, drainage points, seams, flashings, gutters, and concealed fastening details to reduce leakage risk in industrial roofing projects.
hero.visual_direction: industrial roof detail, standing seam profile, drainage/flashing technical overlay

problem_context.title: Roof Leakage Is Usually a Design Coordination Problem.
cards: Weak drainage planning
Incorrect flashing details
Poor seam coordination
Improper fastener exposure
Expansion and movement not considered
Installation sequence errors

steps.title: Roof Geometry Review
steps.description: Slope, roof spans, drainage paths, penetrations, gutters, and edge conditions are reviewed before execution.

steps.title: Waterproofing Detail Coordination
steps.description: Seams, overlaps, flashings, ridges, valleys, and connection details are coordinated to reduce leakage risk.

steps.title: Material and Accessory Planning
steps.description: Roof sheets, clips, fasteners, flashings, gutters, and drainage accessories are planned before site work.

steps.title: Controlled Roof Installation
steps.description: Installation follows technical sequencing and quality checkpoints for waterproofing performance.

faq.question: Why is standing seam roofing used for industrial projects?
faq.answer: It supports concealed fastening, controlled seams, and improved waterproofing logic for large industrial roofs.

faq.question: What causes most industrial roof leakage?
faq.answer: Leakage often comes from weak drainage planning, poor flashing details, incorrect penetrations, or installation errors.

faq.question: Does SIPANEL review drainage before installation?
faq.answer: Yes. Drainage paths, gutters, downspouts, slopes, and critical waterproofing details are reviewed before execution.

conversion_cta.headline: Before Roofing Starts, Review the Leakage Risk.
conversion_cta.text: Request a roof engineering review for drainage, flashing, and execution coordination.

faq.question: How is leakage risk controlled in skylight installations?

faq.question: Can SIPANEL help select the right daylighting material?
faq.answer: Yes. Material selection is reviewed based on light transmission needs, UV exposure, thermal performance, structural loads, and project budget.
